gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the big-field-of-view scanners cost: at US reseller SKYLAB3D the marker-free SHINING 3D FreeScan Trak Nova system ($49,999, tracker plus the UE Nova scanner) is listed $401 below the UE Nova scanner alone ($50,400, markers needed), while the FreeScan Omni ($38,999) covers about 1/4.3 of the Nova's 2.6 x 2.2 m frame and the Trak ProW+ is $135,000.
standout_why: Compared against the cited rivals rev1tech.com 'Shining 3D FreeScan Lineup Compared (2026 Guide)' (no prices, every model routed to 'Get a Quote'), 3dwonders.com 'Best 3D Scanner for Automotive Inspection in 2026' (no prices for Omni, UE Pro2 or Trak Nova; only 'premium price point') and 3dwonders.com 'Best 3D Scanner for Large-Scale Dimensional Inspection in 2026' (prices only the FreeScan Combo $11,999 / Combo+ $14,999, neither a large-FOV pick). ChatGPT's own answers priced only the Artec Leo ($34,505.78), the Creality RaptorX ($4,599) and the Trak ProW+ (~$135,000 via SKYLAB3D); none priced the Trak Nova, UE Nova, Omni or SIMSCAN-E, and none set price against field of view.
decides: Confirms the FreeScan Trak Nova as the pick for a big car part and removes the UE Nova as a cheaper 'rapid coverage' alternative (ChatGPT's #2 in chat 1): at the same reseller it costs more than the Trak Nova system, has the same 2,600 x 2,200 mm frame, and still needs markers. The Omni (ChatGPT's 'best high-speed handheld') is $11,000 less but its largest frame is about 4.3 times smaller, so more passes on a door or hood. The Trak ProW+ is 2.7x the Trak Nova's price for a bigger single-station volume that a single car part does not need. Below $5,000 (RaptorX $3,299, EINSTAR VEGA $1,499, Revopoint MetroX Pro $846) nothing sourced offers a comparable frame size.

Arithmetic: UE Nova + upgrade = $68,399, $18,400 more than the Trak Nova package; UE Nova alone is $401 more than the Trak Nova package.
